questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Somebody has stolen my register.

options.text: My register has been stolen upon.
My register has stolen by somebody.
My register has been a steal.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **My register has been stolen.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**:-

__
 
• The given sentence is in **active voice**.
 
• The active voice is in **present perfect tense**.
 
• Whenever an active voice is given in present perfect tense, we change it according to the following structure:-
 
 
• Active Voice -** Subject + has/have + V₃ + Object.**
 
• Passive Voice - **Object + has/have + been + V₃ + Subject.**
 
 
 
• **For Example:-**
 
 
• Active Voice - This man **has washed** the clothes.
 
• Passive Voice - The clothes **have been washed** by this man.
 
 
 
• Here,** 'this man'**(i.e. the subject) has become the object and the **'clothes'**(i.e. the object has become the subject).
 
• In the question sentence **'my register' **is the object and** 'somebody'** is the subject.
 
• Therefore,** 'my register' **has become the subject and** 'somebody'** has become the object.

**Thus, the correct passive voice of the given active voice is** *My register has been stolen.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When we convert active voice to passive voice, three things need to be kept in mind:-

 
 
• Change object into subject.
 
• Change subject into object.
 
• Always use third form of verb in passive voice.
 
• Use 'by' before the new object.

questions.question: In Microsoft Word, ______ view shows how the document would look when it is printed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Print Layout.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The print layout **will help to show what the document will look like when it is actually printed.
 
• In the print layout, we can see the **page breaks and the other features** as well as the basic paragraph **formatting and the basic character.**
 
• It is also helpful to see where the text or paragraph ends on the page or breaks over two pages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Web layout**

 
 
• **Web layout view** enables us to view our document as **it would appear in a web browser such as Internet Explorer.**
 
• In the Web layout view, the** text appears to fit the window instead of the page margins. **
 
• Background colours and images inserted in the document are also visible.
 
 
 
• **Reading**** view** is optimized for **reading** a document on the computer screen and you also have the option of seeing the document as it would appear on a printed page.
